incidents-bot: PAGER: HIGH — potential cross-tenant KV read detected on Dedicated pool dp-helio-03 (customer: HelioHealth). Alert: unexpected GETs for tenant prefix /helio/ appearing in logs for pool assigned to cust:vestra. Please acknowledge. Pager -> @Sanjay @Mia Chen @Alex R <https://internal/alerts/1769012345>

Mia Chen: acknowledged. jumping in. any customer impact reported? :eyes:

Sanjay Patel: I saw a spike in get requests hitting dp-helio-03 ~ 23:04 UTC, some keys returned values with helio prefix while src tenant is vestra. no confirmed leak yet. marking impact as potential cross-tenant read. paging infra.

Alex R: oncall commands I'm running quick check now — listing active namespaces on that pool.

Alex R: ```
# query pool metadata
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://infra.internal/pools/dp-helio-03/namespaces | jq .
# recent kv audit
kubectl logs -n inference dp-helio-03 --tail=200 | grep "GET /helio/" | tail -n 40
```

Priya Das: tagging security and SRE. @security on call: please watch for PII exposure. We'll avoid broad communication until confirmed.

ops-bot: Automated snapshot created: s3://redwood-incidents/1769012345/dp-helio-03-logs.tar.gz

Sanjay Patel: I ran a sample of logs. snippet:

```
2026-03-14T23:03:22Z INFO kv.get tenant=vestra key=/helio/patient_123 resp_len=204
2026-03-14T23:03:22Z INFO kv.get tenant=vestra key=/helio/patient_456 resp_len=198
```

Mia Chen: that's the smoking gun pattern. keys include helio prefix but tenant is vestra. could be routing config or KV prefix collision in the dedicated pool overlay.

Alex R: immediate mitigation proposal: 1) evict dp-helio-03 from serving helio and vestra traffic (isolate), 2) flip pool to read-only for a minute (prevent further reads), 3) capture in-flight requests. Thoughts?

Sanjay Patel: do (1) and (2) now. I'll collect kvcache contents and dump eviction metrics.

incidents-bot: ACTION: evict-job started by @Mia Chen for pool dp-helio-03. Job ID ej-1769012345

Mia Chen: running evict command: ```
infractl pool isolate dp-helio-03 --tenant-binding temporary --reason "suspected-cross-tenant-read"
infractl pool set-mode dp-helio-03 --mode read-only
```

Priya Das: set up retention for detailed logs and toggled enhanced audit for the pool. also creating a secure share to upload any extracted values for redaction review.

Alex R: extracting KV cache snapshot now. command:

```
redis-cli -h dp-helio-03-cache --rdb /tmp/cache-dump-1769012345.rdb
scp /tmp/cache-dump-1769012345.rdb buildkite:/tmp/secure-upload
```

ops-bot: Eviction completed. dp-helio-03 removed from router maps at 23:07 UTC. Pool now in read-only mode.

Sanjay Patel: pulled matching request traces. correlation id list: ["cid-7b9","cid-8d2","cid-9aa"]. I'm attaching a sanitized snippet to the secure share.

Mia Chen: customer comms: HelioHealth SRE pinged via secure channel; they acknowledge issue and requested a timeline. I'm drafting an initial notification: "We detected anomalous reads within the dedicated pool serving your account. We have isolated the pool and are investigating. No confirmed external disclosure yet; we will share findings within 4 hours." Approve?

Priya Das: approve. add 'no confirmed evidence of PII at this time' but mention logs preserved and our forensic steps.

Alex R: root cause hypothesis so far: router prefix map had stale binding: a recent config change for vestra's routing rule introduced a wildcard that matched /helio/ prefixes for a subset of nodes. Combined with an async namespace deletion path, cache entries were not purged and were served. Need config diff and commit history.

Mia Chen: can someone grab git diff of router rules for pool dp-helio-03 since 2026-03-12? `git log --since="2026-03-12" infra/router-config`

Sanjay Patel: grabbing diffs now. I see a merge from feature/vestra-route that added `path_prefix: /` with an allowlist that didn't include explicit tenant scoping. looks suspicious.

incidents-bot: NOTE: Please tag #legal if you find any customer data. Evidence retention policy applies.

Priya Das: next steps and owner list: evidence collection (Sanjay), config rollback (Alex), customer comms (Mia), security review (Priya). I'll create runbook tasks and a follow-up meeting at +30.

Alex R: I'm preparing a rollback patch. patch:

```
- path_prefix: /
+ path_prefix: /vestra/
+ tenant_scope: vestra
```

Mia Chen: rolling back route change will require a short routing update — estimate 2m to push and propagate. Approving immediate rollback.

Sanjay Patel: extracted cache entries show ~12 keys that map to helio prefixes. cross-checking values now. if they contain PII we'll escalate.

ops-bot: Router config updated: infra/router-config commit a9f3d -> rolled back to a9d9c. Propagation started.

Alex R: propagation reports: 50% nodes updated after 60s, 100% after 2m. verifying no further GETs for /helio/ from vestra.

Mia Chen: monitoring — logs show no new GETs from tenant vestra for /helio/ after rollback. good.

Sanjay Patel: preliminary forensic: values look like app-level test data, no full PII fields present. we'll await security's deeper scan.

Priya Das: security says preliminary scan passed, no sensitive PII detected. still treat as high severity and conduct full audit.

Mia Chen: transitioning to post-mitigation handoff. On-call shift change in 10m — @Alex R will take lead for evidence packaging and remediation follow-up. @Sanjay put your notes in the incident doc.

Alex R: acknowledged. I'll own follow-ups and coordinate with platform for stronger tenant scoping validation. tagging @eng-runtime for long-term fix.

Sanjay Patel: uploading artifacts to secure share s3://redwood-incidents/1769012345/artifacts. checklist in incident doc updated.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigated) — pool isolated & route rollback applied. severity: P1 -> P1 (investigation ongoing). Timeline and artifacts: https://internal/incidents/1769012345

Mia Chen: final notes: action items:
- retro within 48h (owner: Mia Chen)
- add automated test to block wildcard path_prefix without tenant_scope (owner: Alex R)
- increase KV cache purge on namespace unbind (owner: SRE team)
- customer follow-up scheduled in 4 hours (Mia)

Priya Das: leaving note for legal and compliance to review artifact set. if anything changes ping #security immediately.

Alex R: handing over to next on-call for evidence packaging. I'm adding runbook entries and linking PRs.

Mia Chen: thanks team. good mitigation speed. closing Slack handoff. :heart:
